actions.name: compromise a business email account
actions.description: A cyber criminal initially compromises a business email account through social engineering or computer intrusion techniques.

actions.name: conduct reconnaissance on the victim’s email communications
actions.description: Following the initial intrusion, the cyber criminal uses the system access to conduct reconnaissance on the victim’s email communications.

actions.name: create auto-forwarding rules within email accounts
actions.description: BEC actors create auto-forwarding rules within email accounts after they obtain employee credentials to decrease the victims’ ability to observe fraudulent communications.

actions.name: update auto-forwarding email rules in the web-based client
actions.description: After obtaining access to a victim’s email account, cyber criminals update the auto-forwarding email rules in the web-based client.

actions.name: conceal auto-forwarding rules from desktop client and security administrators
actions.description: The web-based client’s forwarding rules often do not sync with the desktop client, limiting the rules’ visibility to cyber security administrators, which cyber criminals capitalize on to increase the likelihood of a successful BEC.

actions.name: impersonate an employee over email communications to redirect payments
actions.description: Using information gathered from the compromised accounts and reconnaissance efforts, the cyber criminal impersonates an employee over email communications to redirect pending or future payments to fraudulent bank accounts.

actions.name: use auto-forwarding rules to delete records from the recycle bin
actions.description: Cyber criminals may also use auto-forwarding rules to delete records from the recycle bin to further obfuscate their activities.

actions.name: create auto-forwarding email rules on the recently upgraded web client
actions.description: In August 2020, cyber criminals created auto-forwarding email rules on the recently upgraded web client of a US-based medical equipment company. The webmail did not sync to the desktop application and went unnoticed by the victim company.

actions.name: impersonate a known international vendor using a similar domain
actions.description: After obtaining access to the network, the actors impersonated a known international vendor by creating a domain with similar spelling to the victim and communicated with the vendor using a UK-based IP address to increase the likelihood of payment.

actions.name: obtain $175,000 from the victim
actions.description: The actors obtained $175,000 from the victim.

actions.name: create three forwarding rules within the web-based email
actions.description: In another incident in August 2020, the same actor created three forwarding rules within the web-based email used by a manufacturing company.

actions.name: auto-forward emails with specific search terms to the cyber criminal’s email address
actions.description: The first rule auto-forwarded any emails with the search terms "bank," "payment," "invoice," "wire," or "check" to the cyber criminal’s email address.

actions.name: auto-forward emails based on sender's domain to the cyber criminal’s email address
actions.description: The other two rules were based off the sender's domain and again forwarded to the same email address.
